source.title: Hackaday.io: Steadywin GIM6010-8 vs Xiaomi CyberGear micromotor

notRanked: The log puts the 3 N·m stall down to the ODrive Micro's current limit, so it measures the driver setup rather than the actuator. Shown, but not set against the datasheet.
methodNote: A second-hand stall figure: the log quotes another builder's measurement and gives no rig. The log's own test compares current at a fixed load (2.29 A here, 1.99 A for a CyberGear). The log states no uncertainty: ±1 N·m is our estimate, wide because the figure is second-hand and the rig unknown.
plausibilityNote: 3 N·m is 0.27x the 11 N·m rating. The log suspects the ODrive Micro's current limit, so this says more about the driver setup than the actuator.
note: Weak evidence, kept because it is the only published stall test we found. A run with a stated current limit would replace it.
